cards.front: Recall a key point about Telescopes & Instruments
cards.back: Refracting telescopes use a convex objective lens to gather and focus light

cards.front: Recall a key point about Telescopes & Instruments
cards.back: Reflecting telescopes use a concave primary mirror; Newtonian and Cassegrain are common designs

cards.front: Recall a key point about Telescopes & Instruments
cards.back: Magnification = focal length of objective / focal length of eyepiece

cards.front: Recall a key point about Telescopes & Instruments
cards.back: Resolving power is the ability to distinguish fine detail; larger apertures give better resolution

cards.front: Recall a key point about Telescopes & Instruments
cards.back: Radio telescopes use large dish antennas to detect radio wavelengths; they can observe day and night

cards.front: Recall a key point about Telescopes & Instruments
cards.back: Space telescopes (e.g. Hubble, JWST) avoid atmospheric distortion and observe wavelengths blocked by the atmosphere

cards.front: What should you know about gcse astronomy exam tips — telescopes & instruments?
cards.back: 1. For Telescopes & Instruments questions, define key terms before explaining processes 2. Use 'because' to link cause and effect in your explanations 3. Include units in all calculations and show your working for method marks 4. When evaluating Telescopes & Instruments, consider both the quality of evidence and practical implications 5. cards.front: Understanding Telescopes & Instruments in GCSE Astronomy
cards.back: Telescopes & Instruments is a key topic in GCSE Astronomy (AQA 8463 / Edexcel 1AS0) that requires understanding of both observational astronomy and theoretical concepts. You must be able to describe astronomical phenomena, explain the physical processes behind them, and apply mathematical relationships to solve astronomical problems.
